name: openstation-electron-adapter
//type: Deliberately CommonJS. Electron's main process and preloads load `app/dist/**` as CJS; declaring the package as an ES module would break them. The build configs carry `.mjs` / `.mts` extensions instead.
description: Sets OpenStation windows free into real OS windows. A WordPress plugin (shell adapter) plus the Electron host app that opens the windows.

scripts.build: npm run build:shell && npm run build:app
scripts.build:shell: vite build --mode development && vite build --mode production
scripts.build:app: tsc -p app/tsconfig.json && npm run build:connect && node scripts/copy-renderer.mjs
scripts.start: npm run brand:dev && npm run build:app && electron .
scripts.verify: npm run build && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test

//overrides: `@wordpress/eslint-plugin` pins an old `@typescript-eslint`, which pins a `minimatch` with a ReDoS advisory. Nothing here feeds user input to a glob — the only patterns are our own lint globs — but the fix is a one-line override rather than waiting upstream, so there is no reason to carry it. Drop this once the plugin's own tree moves.

build.//icons: build/icon.icns and build/icon.png are generated from .wordpress-org/icon.svg and committed, so packaging never needs a rasteriser installed. electron-builder derives the Windows .ico and the Linux sizes from the 1024px PNG.
